hints: Work done against friction is the friction force multiplied by the distance moved along the plane.
Multiply the friction force $40\text{ N}$ by the distance $15\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for work done against a constant resistive force:
$$W = F_{\text{friction}} \times d$$

Substitute the friction force $F_{\text{friction}} = 40\text{ N}$ and distance along the incline $d = 15\text{ m}$:
$$W = 40 \times 15 = 600\text{ J}$$

hints: Change in gravitational potential energy is given by $\Delta E_p = mgh$.
Find the vertical height gained: $h = d\sin 20^\circ = 15\sin 20^\circ$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for change in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh$$

The box moves a distance $d = 15\text{ m}$ up a plane inclined at $20^\circ$. The vertical rise $h$ is:
$$h = d\sin 20^\circ = 15\sin 20^\circ$$

Substitute mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ and acceleration due to gravity $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$\Delta E_p = 5 \times 10 \times 15\sin 20^\circ = 750\sin 20^\circ$$

hints: Since the speed is constant, there is no change in kinetic energy.
The work done by the pulling force equals the work done against friction plus the gain in gravitational potential energy.
walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle for motion at constant speed (where $\Delta E_k = 0$):
$$W_{\text{pulling}} = W_{\text{friction}} + \Delta E_p$$

Substitute the values obtained in parts (a) and (b):
$$W_{\text{pulling}} = 600 + 256.515 = 856.515\text{ J} \approx 857\text{ J}$$
